applied.summary: Atomic replace (temp-file then rename) is named in R5's own DF2.1 title and R4 §3.2 as first-class run-record discipline, but lived only in Technical Notes and INV-3 with no AC and no test. Folded into AC2 as a testable clause (failure injected between write and rename leaves the prior record byte-identical, no .tmp residue) and retitled the DoD unit test to 'Test (atomic replace + idempotent close)', keeping DoD at the 10-item cap.

The run id becomes both the record filename and, via the box name, a public hostname, yet the hostname grammar / 63-char / never-supplied guard existed only in Guards-limits with no AC. Added AC6 placing the guard at path() — the single id-to-path chokepoint every verb routes through — rather than at newId() only, so create/get/set/close/path all reject ../evil, A-b and 64+ chars before a path is built. Extended the create-path DoD test to cover it. Fires input-invariants path-handling and server-generated-storage-key items on a write path.

E2E Slice enumerated six lifecycle verbs (create through teardown) while AC5 and the MANDATORY DoD e2e demo both said 'all seven' — an internal contradiction on the exact verb set other DF2/DF3 stories build against. Added reap to the demo chain; the set now matches the shared pattern note exactly.

copyFile(vm, remotePath, localPath) left transfer direction unspecified, and DF2.5 depends on it to pull the bundle and artifacts tar down. Pinned to box-to-host only and tied the rationale to DF2.3 delivering the run key on exec stdin, so the seam itself forbids pushing a file into a box. Verified copyFile appears in no story outside these two files, so no cross-story rename risk.

Overview claimed 'six command shapes across five files'; R4 §3.5 puts whoami in a sixth file (manage/mod.just) — five files carry the operational five. Dropped the file count, which line 99 already stated correctly.

INV-5 states three fail-closed conditions (git bundle verify unavailable at preflight, bundle fails verification, driver cannot confirm box destruction) and none had an AC or a test — in the one story whose stated premise is that the reference shipped teardown unrun (R4 §3.6, teardown_and_reap.md:6). Verify-fails is covered transitively by AC3; preflight-unavailable and unconfirmed-destroy were not. Added AC6 and merged a fail-closed assertion into the ordering DoD test, keeping DoD at 10.

--no-harvest appeared in the Trigger Surface and Technical Notes as the explicit opt-out from AC3's abort guard — the one irreversible-mistake path — with no AC defining its behavior. Scoped in AC6: it waives AC3's harvest gate only, never the INV-5 stops, and the waiver goes to the run log, never the record (keeping DF2.1's twelve-field schema closed).

The 512 MiB caps were measured on the received archive only, with nothing stating the artifacts tar is uncompressed — a compressed bomb from a skip-permissions agent could fill the host disk, which per R5 §6 fact 11 is a 100GB pooled resource. Guards now require the cap on summed entry sizes before extraction (an uncompressed-total cap) and explicitly reject escaping-symlink entries alongside absolute-path and .. entries. Fires input-invariants expanded-size-cap and symlink-safety items.

surviving.summary: The tolerance 'trace DB and artifacts absence is logged and does not abort harvest' lives only in the Infra Prerequisites table with no AC. AC4 covers the zero-commit no-op but not a missing tar member. Not fixed: DF2.5 sits at 199/200 normative lines with DoD at the 10-item cap, so adding it would require cutting binding content. Low blast radius — the behavior is stated normatively and is graceful degradation, not a security path.

The per-field coercion map coerces ports via json from argv with no shape or size bound stated. Operator-supplied rather than agent-supplied, so it sits inside the trust boundary, but a malformed or oversized ports value has no defined rejection behavior.

reap is in scope as a seam verb (Technical Notes, AC5, and now the E2E demo) while the Trigger Surface marks 'fleet-wide reaper walking list()' out-of-scope to DF2.6. Both statements are correct and the table wording is precise, but the tension reads as a contradiction on first pass.

Teardown is specified as six steps against the reference's seven (R4 §3.6) — the seventh, gating on key absence from the authoritative list, is correctly delegated to DF2.3's verify verb per the Boundaries bullet. Correct as written, but a reader diffing against R4 §3.6 will pause on the step count.
